title: 开发板：供电和 GPIO
summary: 把 ESP32 开发板插上面包板，用它给电源轨供电，再把一个引脚设成输出点亮 LED、另一个设成输入读按键。
concepts: pin current limit 引脚电流
description: 开发板插在面包板上，每个引脚只剩 a 行或 j 行一个空孔。这里没有程序：每个 GPIO 在「属性」里选一个模式，模式就是程序。输出高 ≈ 3.3 V 串 25 Ω；输入只听不出力，按键要配上拉。
compare:
**对比**：
- 3V3 脚 ≈ 3.3 V；5V 脚 ≈ 5 V − 0.3 V ≈ **4.7 V**；
- LED 电流 = (3.3 − 1.8) V / (330 + 25 + 12) Ω ≈ **4.1 mA**（25 Ω 是引脚输出电阻，12 Ω 是 LED 内阻）；
- 引脚电压 = 3.3 V − 25 Ω × 4.1 mA ≈ **3.20 V**；由此算出输出电阻 ≈ **25 Ω**；
- 上拉输入：松开读高，按下读低（按下时引脚被按键接到 GND，上拉电阻里流过 3.3 V / 45 kΩ ≈ 73 µA）。

en.title: The dev board: power and GPIO
en.summary: Plug an ESP32 board into the breadboard, power the rails from it, then make one pin an output that lights an LED and another an input that reads a button.
en.description: The board sits on the breadboard with one free hole per pin, in row a or row j. There is no program here: each GPIO gets a mode under Properties, and the mode is the program. Output high ≈ 3.3 V behind 25 Ω; an input only listens, so a button needs a pull-up.
steps: Pick **ESP32 DevKitC** and click **`b1`** (the GND pin at the top left). The pin rows go into `b1`–`b19` and `i1`–`i19`. USB is plugged in by default, so the board is powered. Hover a pin to see its name.
Power the bottom rails from the board: red jumper **`j1`** → **`bp1`** (the 3V3 pin), blue jumper **`j14`** → **`bn14`** (a GND pin). The bottom red rail is now 3.3 V.
The top GND rail too: blue jumper **`a7`** → **`tn7`** (column 7 of the upper row is another GND pin).
**Multimeter**: red probe on **`bp5`** (the 3V3 rail), then on **`j19`** (the 5V pin). What does each read?
LED circuit: a **resistor** of `330 Ω` from **`a15`** (GPIO2) to **`a22`**.
**Red LED**, long lead in **`c22`**, short lead in **`c25`**; blue jumper **`a25`** → **`tn25`** (GND). The LED is wired — is it lit?
**Click the board** and, in the pin list under Properties, set **GPIO2** to **OUT HIGH**. The LED lights. The row also shows the pin voltage and the current flowing out.
**Push button**: pick it and click **`e27`**. It straddles the trench: one side on column 27, the other on column 29.
Jumper **`a13`** → **`a27`** (GPIO4 to one side of the button), blue jumper **`j29`** → **`bn29`** (the other side to GND).

GPIO4 is a plain input now. With the button released it reads "floating", and Diagnostics says so. Set **GPIO4** to **IN pull-up**: it reads "high". **Click the button** with Select / use to press it: "low".
Press **Check my circuit**, then answer the questions with the multimeter and the pin list.
hints: Each pin has one free hole, in row a (upper row) or row j (lower row); hover a pin to see its name.
Output high = 3.3 V behind 25 Ω: LED current = (3.3 − LED drop) / (R + 25 Ω + the LED's 12 Ω).
Pulled-up input: pulled to 3.3 V when released, tied to GND by the button when pressed.
tests: Output high: LED on; button released reads high

measurements.explain: The USB 5 V passes a Schottky diode first and loses about 0.3 V.

measurements.ask: The LED current (click the GPIO2 row to see the pin current, or put an ammeter in series)
measurements.explain: (3.3 − 1.8) V / (330 + 25 + 12) Ω ≈ 4.1 mA, well under the recommended 20 mA.
The output resistance drops 25 Ω × 4.1 mA ≈ 0.1 V.

measurements.ask: From your readings, the pin's output resistance: (3.3 V − pin voltage) / current
measurements.explain: About 25 Ω. At 20 mA the pin would be down to about 2.8 V — heavy loads need a transistor or MOSFET driver (phase 5 labs).

measurements.ask: GPIO4 set to input with pull-up: what does it read with the button pressed?
choices: low: the button ties the pin to GND; the pull-up can only supply a tiny current
measurements.explain: Released, the pull-up holds the pin at 3.3 V (high); pressed, the pin is tied to GND (low). This is called active-low.

cards.title: Plug in the board, wire an LED
text: Plug the **ESP32 board** into the breadboard and power the rails from its supply pins.
Then wire an **LED** through a resistor from one pin. Follow the steps below; each one is checked automatically.
Last, look closely: the LED is wired to a pin — **so why is it dark**?

cards.title: A pin's mode is its program
text: - This board runs no code. Each pin (**GPIO**) gets a **mode** under Properties, and the mode is the program.
- A pin you have not set is an **input**: it only "listens" and drives nothing. That is why the LED is dark.
- Set to **output high**, the pin acts like a 3.3 V battery with a small resistance of about 25 Ω in series. The more current flows, the more voltage that small resistance takes:
![](fig:out)
- With numbers: a red LED with 150 Ω gives $I = \frac{3.3 - 1.8}{150 + 25 + 12} ≈ 0.008$ A, that is 8 mA.

- An input with nothing attached is **floating**, and its reading jumps around. A **pull-up** is a resistor of about 45 kΩ inside the chip that gently pulls the pin to 3.3 V; pressing the button ties it straight to GND.
![](fig:pullup)

cards.title: Make it an output, then read a button
text: - **Click the board** and change modes in the pin list under Properties: first make GPIO2 output high.
- Then wire a button, set GPIO4 to IN pull-up, and press it to see the reading change.
- Predict first: your resistor is 330 Ω, more than twice the 150 Ω in the example above. What current will you get?

cards.title: Take away
text: - **The 3V3, 5V and GND pins can all power the breadboard.** The 5V pin is a little under USB's 5 V: a Schottky diode sits in between.
- **Output high ≈ 3.3 V behind 25 Ω**: the more current, the lower the pin voltage. Keep each pin ≤ 20 mA; above 40 mA it is damaged — an LED always needs a resistor.
- **An input only listens**: with nothing attached it floats, so a button needs a pull-up or a pull-down.
- A real-board catch: many pins have other jobs (boot configuration, the serial port, GPIO6–11 wired to the flash). Check the board's pinout before you use one.

tests.name: 输出高：LED 亮；松开按键读高

measurements.ask: 万用表：5V 脚（j19）对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: USB 的 5 V 先经过肖特基二极管，掉了约 0.3 V。

measurements.ask: LED 的电流（单击 GPIO2 那一行看引脚电流，或者串一个电流表）
万用表：GPIO2（a15）对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 输出电阻上掉了 25 Ω × 4.1 mA ≈ 0.1 V。

measurements.ask: 用你的读数算引脚的输出电阻：(3.3 V − 引脚电压) / 电流
measurements.explain: 约 25 Ω。电流 20 mA 时引脚只剩约 2.8 V——大电流负载要用三极管或 MOSFET 驱动（第 5 期实验）。

measurements.ask: GPIO4 设成“输入 上拉”，按下按键时读到什么？
choices: 低：按键把引脚接到 GND，上拉电阻只能提供很小的电流
measurements.explain: 松开时上拉把引脚拉到 3.3 V（高）；按下时引脚直接接 GND（低）。这叫“低电平有效”。

steps.text: 选**「ESP32 开发板 DevKitC」**，单击 **`b1`**（左上角的 GND 脚）。两排针插在 `b1`–`b19` 和 `i1`–`i19`。USB 默认插着，板子已经通电。鼠标停在针脚上能看到名字。
下方电源轨接到板子上：红色跳线 **`j1`** → **`bp1`**（3V3 脚），蓝色跳线 **`j14`** → **`bn14`**（GND 脚）。下方红轨现在是 3.3 V。
上方 GND 轨也接上：蓝色跳线 **`a7`** → **`tn7`**（上排第 7 列也是 GND 脚）。
**万用表**：红表笔先点 **`bp5`**（3V3 轨），再点 **`j19`**（5V 脚）。两个读数各是多少？
**红色 LED** 长脚插 **`c22`**、短脚插 **`c25`**；蓝色跳线 **`a25`** → **`tn25`**（GND）。LED 接好了——它亮吗？
**单击开发板**，在「属性」的引脚列表里把 **GPIO2** 设成**「输出 高」**。LED 亮了。这一行还显示引脚电压和流出的电流。
**按键**：选「按键开关」，单击 **`e27`**。它横跨中间的凹槽：一边在第 27 列，另一边在第 29 列。
跳线 **`a13`** → **`a27`**（GPIO4 接按键一边），蓝色跳线 **`j29`** → **`bn29`**（按键另一边接 GND）。
GPIO4 现在是普通输入。松开按键时它读「浮空」，「诊断」里也有提示。把 **GPIO4** 设成**「输入 上拉」**：读「高」。用「选择 / 操作」**单击按键**按下它：读「低」。
点**「检查我的电路」**，再用万用表和引脚列表回答测量题。

hints: 每个引脚只剩 a 行（上排）或 j 行（下排）一个空孔能接线；鼠标停在针脚上看名字。
输出高 = 3.3 V 串 25 Ω：LED 电流 = (3.3 − LED 压降) / (R + 25 Ω + LED 内阻 12 Ω)。
上拉输入：松开时被拉到 3.3 V，按下时被按键接到 GND。

cards.title: 插上板子，接一颗灯
text: 把 **ESP32 开发板**插上面包板，用它的电源脚给电源轨供电。
然后从一个引脚经过电阻接一颗 **LED**，照着下面的步骤做，每一步都会自动检查。
最后看一眼：LED 明明接在引脚上了，**为什么不亮**？

cards.title: 引脚的模式就是程序
text: - 这里的开发板不跑代码。每个引脚（**GPIO**）在「属性」里选一个**模式**，模式就是程序。
- 没设过的引脚是**输入**：它只“听”，不出力。所以 LED 不亮。
- 设成**输出高**以后，引脚就像一节 3.3 V 电池，串着一个约 25 Ω 的小电阻。电流越大，这个小电阻上掉的电压越多：
![](fig:out)
- 输入什么都不接时叫**浮空**，读数乱跳。**上拉**是芯片里一个约 45 kΩ 的电阻，把引脚轻轻拉到 3.3 V；按键一按，就把它直接接到 GND。
![](fig:pullup)

cards.title: 设成输出，再读一个按键
text: - **单击开发板**，在「属性」的引脚列表里改模式：先让 GPIO2 输出高。
- 再接一个按键，把 GPIO4 设成「输入 上拉」，按一下看读数怎么变。
- 先预测：你的电阻是 330 Ω，比上面例子里的 150 Ω 大一倍多，电流会是多少？

cards.title: 带走
text: - **3V3、5V、GND 脚都能给面包板供电。** 5V 脚比 USB 的 5 V 低一点：中间隔着一只肖特基二极管。
- **输出高 ≈ 3.3 V 串 25 Ω**：电流越大，引脚电压越低。每个引脚建议 ≤ 20 mA，超过 40 mA 会损坏——LED 一定要串电阻。
- **输入只听不出力**：什么都不接就浮空，按键要配上拉或下拉。
- 真实板子上的坑：很多引脚另有用途（启动配置、串口、接 Flash 的 GPIO6–11）。用之前先查开发板的引脚图。

caption.text: 引脚输出高 = 3.3 V 串 25 Ω：这两样都在芯片里面。电流 I 依次穿过 25 Ω、R1 和 LED。

i18n.en: Output high = 3.3 V behind 25 Ω, both inside the chip. The current I passes 25 Ω, R1 and the LED in turn.

caption.text: 上拉：松开时，45 kΩ 把 GPIO4 拉到 3.3 V（读高）；按下时，按键把它直接接到 GND（读低）。

i18n.en: Pull-up: released, 45 kΩ pulls GPIO4 to 3.3 V (reads high); pressed, the button ties it straight to GND (reads low).
